findings.check: REQ-001 / R2: a line in the journal exists only because of a hook firing or a fresh signed record; ISS-0123 sibling place (note path)
findings.title: A signed note body is accepted again after 120 seconds, at any later time, and each time appends a new ORCH record
findings.where: tools/src/pixel-office/server.js lines 192-206 (REPLAY_KEEP_MS = 2 * WRITE_SKEW_MS, replayed()) and 372-395 (processNote); tools/src/pixel-office/protocol.js line 322 (a note body may not carry time)
findings.evidence: Probe on the head, a test server on port 0 with a clock that the test moves, one signed note body sent four times. Output: note_1 -> 200 {request_time:2026-11-22T12:00:00.000Z,request_time_auto:true}; note_replay_t+10s -> 409 {error:replayed}; note_replay_t+210s -> 200; note_replay_t+30d -> 200. The journal read afterwards holds three ORCH records with the same note_text and the times 12:00:00, 12:03:30 and 2026-12-22T12:03:30, each bound to the same owner message. Cause by reading: a hook body carries its own time, so after 60 s it fails the time check and the 120 s memory is enough; a note body has no time (the server stamps it), so after 120 s nothing refuses it. The tests pin only the inside of the window (pixel-office-server.test.js lines 2041-2058, pixel-office-note.test.js line 545). The closed defect ISS-0123 named this place itself (section on the note path: a captured note body is accepted at any later moment) and its closing record says the cause is removed.
findings.item: R2 (Pixel Office shows only the truth); Q10 (replay); decision 0005
findings.recommendation: Give a note a time that the signature covers and the server checks, the way a hook body has one: the note command adds a time field to the signed body (canonical ISO with milliseconds), validateNoteBody checks it against the clock with WRITE_SKEW_MS, the server still stamps its own record time; or keep the hashes of accepted note bodies for the life of the process. Add a test in tools/test/pixel-office-server.test.js that sends the same signed note body after the window and expects 409 or 400, and fix the closing record of ISS-0123 (open a defect for the part that is not closed). Practical reach is narrow: the attacker needs a captured signed request (a process that took the port of a stopped server, or something that sees the loopback), which is why the audit did not rate it Critical.

findings.check: decision 0005 / tools/README.md (Pixel Office files, rights 0700 and 0600); Q7 (secret closed to other users)
findings.title: On Windows the secret, journal and state folder have no mode protection and the link and owner checks silently do nothing; the README says 0700 and 0600 without a limit
findings.where: tools/src/pixel-office/state-dir.js lines 30, 92, 100 (O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0, getuid check only if present, chmodSync 0o700); journal.js line 37 (NOFOLLOW ?? 0); server.js line 79; tools/README.md (table of the five state files, rights column)
findings.evidence: The tree was moved to this Windows PC. Probe: state folder created by ensureStateDir and ensureSecret in the agent's own folder; the modes read back: dir_mode 666, write-secret 666, events.jsonl 666, port 666, node-path 666, server-starts.jsonl 666 (the README promises 0700 for the folder and 0600 for each file). icacls on write-secret: the access list is inherited from the parent folder (the user, SYSTEM, Administrators and one more principal with read and write), nothing narrowed. In the code: O_NOFOLLOW is undefined on Windows and falls back to 0, so a link in the last component is followed; process.getuid does not exist, so the owner check is skipped; chmodSync does not narrow an ACL and reports no error. git grep for windows and win32 in decisions/0005 and tools/src/pixel-office finds no statement about this. The same code path also lets SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR point to a folder whose ACL is open, and the hook runs the file named in node-path from that folder (hook.sh step 1).
findings.item: Q7; tools/README.md Pixel Office files table; decision 0005
findings.recommendation: Decide whether Windows is a supported place for Pixel Office. If yes: tools/src/pixel-office/state-dir.js checks the ACL (or documents that the folder under the user profile is private by default and refuses a SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR outside it), and tools/README.md says in the table that the modes apply to POSIX only and what protects the secret on Windows. If no: say so in tools/README.md and in decision 0005. Either way add a test that records the behaviour on win32.

findings.check: ISS-0122 (the read key is held only by the owner's browser and the command)
findings.title: The read key is sent to whatever process holds the port during the busy-port probe, and its cookie is not tied to the port
findings.where: tools/src/pixel-office/main.js lines 118-130 (isPixelOffice sends the key header to the occupant of the port); tools/src/pixel-office/server.js line 516 (Set-Cookie with Path=/ and no port scope)
findings.evidence: main.js line 127: headers: { Accept: application/json, [READ_KEY_HEADER]: key } in an http.get to 127.0.0.1:<port> made after EADDRINUSE, before it is known that the occupant is Pixel Office. server.js line 516: the cookie is name=<key>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=31536000. Cookies do not isolate by port, so the browser sends it to every server on 127.0.0.1 (the team page, a dev server). Read by the agent; the probe did not run against a foreign listener.
findings.recommendation: In main.js ask the occupant first without the key (the answer 401 with the body app: sai-pixel-office would need the server to put the marker in the 401 body), then send the key only to a confirmed server; or accept it and name it in tools/README.md. For the cookie, a name with the port in it (sai_pixel_office_4780) limits sending to servers that read that name only, and the key can be shortened in life (Max-Age) to match the use. The key lets one read the masked journal, not write.

summary.text: The write side of Pixel Office holds: loopback only, a Host check, a signature on every write, a time window, one-time bodies for hook events, flat static names, no markup insertion, page that only sends GET, no secret in files and fake-only fixtures, and no writer of events in the project outside the hook and the signed note path. The one real gap is the note path: a signed note body has no time, so the replay guard of ISS-0123 holds for 120 seconds only and the same body is accepted again later (SEC-PO-01, High). On Windows the mode and owner protections of the state folder do nothing and the README does not say so (SEC-PO-02, Medium). The read key goes to the occupant of a busy port during the probe (SEC-PO-03, Low). Four changed files (hook.sh, main.js, note.js, office-report.js) have no test record for the head; they were read, not run.
